articles.title: Alex Rodríguez reveals Derek Jeter's reaction during the famous Sports Illustrated photo shoot
articles.standfirst: The 1997 image became an enduring reminder of Rodríguez and Jeter's early friendship and complicated history
articles.summary: The 1997 image became an enduring reminder of Rodríguez and Jeter's early friendship and complicated history
articles.body:
Alex Rodríguez and Derek Jeter were already emerging as two of baseball’s brightest young stars when they appeared together in one of the sport’s most unusual magazine photographs.

The 1997 Sports Illustrated photo shoot in Miami Beach featured five promising shortstops: Rodríguez, Jeter, Edgar Rentería, Alex González and Rey Ordóñez.

The now-famous image showed the players shirtless, wearing baseball pants and gold chains. What was intended to showcase a talented new generation of infielders eventually became one of the strangest snapshots of their early careers.

Years later, Rodríguez looked back at the photograph with considerably less seriousness. While discussing the shoot, he joked that Jeter had been responsible for the look, saying, “I think that was Derek’s idea. We looked like Menudo. It was a dark moment.”

The comment gave the decades-old photograph another moment in the spotlight, particularly because Rodríguez and Jeter’s relationship would become one of the more complicated friendships in baseball.

In 1997, however, neither player could have known how intertwined their careers would eventually become. Rodríguez was playing for the Seattle Mariners, while Jeter was establishing himself as the Yankees’ shortstop. Both would go on to become franchise icons and among the most recognizable players of their generation.

Their friendship took a significant hit several years later after Rodríguez discussed Jeter during a 2001 Esquire interview. At the time, Rodríguez was with the Texas Rangers and suggested that Jeter had benefited from playing on talented Yankees teams and didn’t have to take on the same leadership burden as other stars.

Jeter later made it clear that the comments bothered him. He said loyalty was extremely important to him and felt that a true friend wouldn’t have made those remarks publicly.

“Those comments bothered me because, like I said, I’m very, very loyal,” Jeter said. “As a friend, I’m loyal. I just looked at it as, ‘I wouldn’t have done it.’

“And then it was the media. The constant hammer to the nail. They just kept hammering it in. It just became noise, which frustrated me. Just constant noise.”

Rodríguez eventually apologized, although he maintained that the substance of what he said was fair.

From young shortstops to Yankees teammates

Despite their complicated history, Rodríguez and Jeter eventually became teammates when Rodríguez joined the Yankees in 2004. Their relationship received plenty of attention in New York, but the pair managed to share the field for several successful seasons.

The partnership reached its high point in 2009, when the Yankees won the World Series. By then, both players had already established themselves as major figures in the sport, making their journey from the 1997 photo shoot to the Bronx particularly remarkable.

Their relationship has also evolved since retirement. Both have appeared together in baseball media, including MLB on Fox, showing that the tension that once surrounded their friendship has softened with time.

That makes Rodríguez’s recent comments about the Sports Illustrated photograph even more entertaining. Jeter may not have escaped the fashion blame, but the image has become a memorable piece of baseball history.

The original shoot was meant to introduce fans to a group of talented young shortstops, but it’s the shirtless photograph that became the lasting image.

Nearly three decades later, Rodríguez can look back and laugh at the awkward styling and youthful confidence.

articles.title: Aaron Boone showers George Lombard Jr. with love and has already moved on from Anthony Volpe
articles.standfirst: The young shortstop made everyone forget about Anthony Volpe almost immediately.
articles.summary: The young shortstop made everyone forget about Anthony Volpe almost immediately.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees roll into Camden Yards looking to lock up a series victory over the Baltimore Orioles following Tuesday's 3-1 win. A primary engine behind New York's recent momentum has been 21-year-old rookie George Lombard Jr. , who continues to reward the organization’s faith since earning his Big League call-up.

Aaron Boone raves about Lombard Jr.’s defense Ahead of Wednesday's matchup, manager Aaron Boone made no secret of his admiration for the young shortstop's transition to the majors.

“I think he’s excellent. I think he’s a great defender… Continues to show that every day he’s up here, but you know, that’s who we’ve kind of known him to be, as he’s come through the minor leagues and, it’s fun to watch him show it at this level.”

Lombard Jr. anchored Tuesday’s victory with a multi-hit performance , finishing with two hits and a run scored to anchor the bottom of the order.

Making waves around the league The rookie's immediate two-way impact has ignited social media and caught the attention of MLB analysts, who have praised his rare combination of defensive poise and offensive consistency at shortstop.

AL East playoff push The Yankees enter Wednesday holding second place in the AL East with a 70-55 record through 125 games . Following the conclusion of their series in Baltimore, New York returns to the Bronx on Friday night to open a pivotal home series against the Toronto Blue Jays .

articles.body:
Yankee Stadium hosts an American League East clash between two teams headed in opposite directions. The New York Yankees arrive as the second-best team in the AL East , with a record of 71 wins and 55 losses (sixth place in Major League Baseball), and a run differential of +89 that confirms the strength of their pitching: they have allowed only 470 runs in 126 games, one of the cleanest defensive records in the entire league.

On the other side, the Toronto Blue Jays are going through a difficult stretch . With 63 wins and 66 losses, they sit in fourth place in the AL East and carry a -49 run differential, the result of an offense that has produced just 513 runs—among the weakest among the contenders—compared to the 562 they have allowed.

On paper, the difference in quality between the two rosters is fully reflected in the market.

articles.title: Aaron Boone can get Cody Bellinger back, but the whole world is waiting for Aaron Judge
articles.standfirst: Yankees get a major boost with Bellinger’s return, but suffer a costly pitching loss at a critical time.
articles.summary: Yankees get a major boost with Bellinger’s return, but suffer a costly pitching loss at a critical time.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees received a major boost on Sunday with the return of Cody Bellinger , who was activated from the injured list and is set to reinforce an offense that has struggled to produce runs in recent weeks.

It wasn't all good news for New York, however. To make room for Bellinger on the roster, pitcher Ryan Weathers was placed on the 15-day injured list with a flexor muscle strain.

New York Yankees' Cody Bellinger

Bellinger's return comes at a crucial time for the Yankees, who are still dealing with several key injuries and hope to welcome back stars like Aaron Judge and Max Fried in the near future.

"I'm very excited," Bellinger said Saturday, according to MLB.com . "I feel good. I'm ready to go."

The outfielder is hitting .259 this season with 11 home runs and 53 RBIs . He had been sidelined with a hamstring strain, an injury he now says he has fully recovered from.

"As the days went on, I was pretty much running at full speed," Bellinger said. "I did defense, and more than you would probably do in a normal game. You just want to make sure you're on your feet for a long period of time."

As for Ryan Weathers , the outlook is also encouraging. Although he was placed on the injured list, the right-hander said he does not believe his season is over.

"Weathers says he doesn't necessarily think this ends his season. Says tests show elbow is fine. Says he dealt with something similar last season in MIA and it kept him out a month, but that was more severe. Says he could have kept pitching but wanted to be smart. No plan yet," The Athletic reported on X Sunday.

At 73-56, the Yankees sit second in the American League East behind the Tampa Bay Rays , but they remain firmly in the division race and hope to build momentum heading into the MLB playoffs .

articles.title: Yankees vs Astros Standings: Previous results in the season and how they enter the series
articles.standfirst: The matchup between Houston and New York in the Bronx promises to be one of the best of the week
articles.summary: The matchup between Houston and New York in the Bronx promises to be one of the best of the week
articles.body:
The 2026 MLB schedule once again brings together two organizations that rarely fail to generate sparks. This Tuesday night, the New York Yankees host the Houston Astros at Yankee Stadium in the Bronx , a matchup between historic powerhouses of the American League’s junior circuit that, however, arrive at this meeting in very different form.

Yankees vs Astros: New York in control, Houston struggling to breathe

The standings snapshot instantly explains the mood in each clubhouse. In the American League East, t he Yankees are in second place with a 73-56 record, only behind the Tampa Bay Rays (76-53).

"It is a team firmly installed in playoff position and with a positive run differential of +95 (571 scored to 476 allowed) , the best defensive mark among the big teams in the East.

On the other side, the Astros arrive with something as unusual for them as it is necessary: leaders of a very tight division . Houston leads the American League West with a 65-65 record, just one game ahead of the Texas Rangers (64-66) and with Seattle right on their heels (62-68).

Their run differential, however, raises alarms: -43 (590 scored against 633 allowed), a symptom of pitching that has bled more than it should in recent weeks .

How are the Yankees and Astros coming into this week games?

Recent form reinforces the sense of crossing paths. The Yankees are coming off a solid road trip : they won part of their series in Baltimore with 3-1, 5-3, and a commanding 6-1 victories, and put together a stretch of seven wins in nine games before splitting their most recent home series against Toronto (3-1 and then 3-4).

New York's hitting has shown power surges —like the 10-5 win over Seattle— without sacrificing its punch in close games, where its bullpen has known how to shut the door.

Houston, meanwhile, has been on a roller coaster . After a strong start to August — including an 11-2 win over Texas — the Astros have gotten tangled up: they lost series to San Diego and Seattle, and their weekend was baffling, with a humiliating 3-18 loss to the Angels followed by a doubleheader against the Athletics in which they won one game 4-0 and lost the other 3-4.

The team alternates convincing shutouts with defensive debacles, and that inconsistency is exactly what New York will want to punish.

What will the lineups be for Yankees vs Astros? Elite rotations and feared bats

If anything guarantees this matchup, it is talent on the mound. The Yankees boast a rotation loaded with elite arms : veteran Gerrit Cole (45), left-hander Max Fried (54) —signed to lead the rotation—, Carlos Rodón (55), and Dominican Luis Gil (81). For the late innings, New York has major bullpen pieces like David Bednar and Dominican Camilo Doval, a tandem capable of locking down any late lead.

Houston responds with its own artillery . Hunter Brown (58) leads a rotation that also includes Japanese pitcher Tatsuya Imai (45), Dominican Ronel Blanco (56), and the experienced Cristian Javier (53). The most feared link, however, remains the back end of the bullpen: left-hander Josh Hader (71), backed by Dominican Bryan Abreu (52), forms one of the most intimidating relief duos in the American League.

At the plate, Houston's offensive balance depends on world-class names : Cuban Yordan Álvarez (44), slotted in as the designated hitter and capable of deciding a game with a single swing, along with first baseman Christian Walker (8) and Dominican catcher Yainer Díaz (21). For New York, catcher Austin Wells (28) has established himself as a key presence behind and at the plate.

What Yankees and Astros need to reach the Playoffs

For the Yankees, every victory is ammunition in their pursuit of Tampa Bay for the top spot in the East and, above all, insurance for their postseason ticket. With the campaign entering its final stretch — both teams have already surpassed 129 games played — keeping pace against American League rivals carries double weight in the tiebreaker criteria.

For Houston, the margin is even narrower. Leading the West Division with a .500 record means that a bad stretch can cost them first place in a matter of days. With Texas just one game back, taking a series in the Bronx—hostile territory by definition—would be a statement that the pitching can hold up away from home, precisely where it has struggled the most.

articles.summary: Lombard Jr.’s recent errors have raised concerns about his development.
articles.body:
George Lombard Jr. has been one of the biggest surprises for the New York Yankees since his promotion to the Major Leagues, but the young shortstop is going through a difficult defensive stretch that has raised some concerns while bringing back memories of Anthony Volpe ’s early struggles at the position.

The 21-year-old prospect has committed four errors over his last four games, a stretch that manager Aaron Boone addressed before Tuesday’s matchup against the Houston Astros , although he downplayed the rookie’s recent struggles.

Aaron Boone backs George Lombard Jr.

“I feel like over time he'll be really good at the routine [plays]. So I think that's just a little bump in the road,” Boone said.

Despite the recent mistakes, the Yankees remain fully confident in Lombard. The organization understands that he is still adapting to the Major League level, especially considering he is only 21 years old and entered Tuesday’s game with just 17 career MLB appearances.

His offensive performance has also been one of the main reasons New York remains so optimistic about his future.

Lombard is hitting .288/.348/.407 in 66 plate appearances and has hit two home runs since reaching the big leagues. While he still has room to improve defensively, his offensive ability has shown that he could become an important piece for the Yankees moving forward.

The Bronx Bombers are currently just 3.5 games behind the Tampa Bay Rays in the race for the division lead, keeping their hopes alive of winning the AL East .

For now, New York’s focus remains on the present: finding consistency during the final stretch of the season and continuing to develop a George Lombard Jr. who, despite his recent mistakes, is still viewed as one of the franchise’s key pieces for the future.

articles.title: Aaron Boone's major headache: The hidden crisis threatening to derail the Yankees' World Series dream
articles.standfirst: Yankees’ World Series hopes could hinge on health as key injuries threaten their postseason run.
articles.summary: Yankees’ World Series hopes could hinge on health as key injuries threaten their postseason run.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees currently lead the American League Wild Card race and sit in second place in the AL East . Barring an unexpected collapse, their postseason berth appears all but secured. Reaching the World Series is also a realistic possibility in an American League that lacks a clear dominant team. However, winning the championship will be a far greater challenge given the strength of the National League contenders, who enter as favorites to capture the Fall Classic.

Still, the Yankees’ biggest opponent may not be on the field, but in the training room. Several key injuries threaten to impact their championship aspirations, beginning with Aaron Judge , although the captain is far from the only player keeping the organization on edge. Here are the five injuries that could shape New York’s path to the 2026 World Series .

Judge continues to recover from a stress fracture of his right first rib , an injury that has sidelined him since early June.

The outlook is encouraging, as the Yankees expect their captain to return before the end of the regular season, giving him time to regain his rhythm ahead of the playoffs.

There is no question that Judge is the team’s most important player. If New York hopes to win its first World Series since 2009, it will need its superstar performing at his best.

The news surrounding Max Fried is far more encouraging. Multiple reports indicate the left-hander could return as soon as this weekend’s series against the Boston Red Sox after recovering from a bone bruise in his left elbow .

Whenever a pitcher is dealing with an elbow injury, teams exercise extreme caution. Still, if there are no setbacks, all signs point to Fried being ready to return.

The rotation has been one of the Yankees’ greatest strengths this season. With Gerrit Cole, Carlos Rodón, and Cam Schlittler leading the staff, adding Fried back into the mix would make New York’s starting rotation one of its most dangerous weapons heading into October.

The situation surrounding Giancarlo Stanton is far more concerning.

The veteran designated hitter was already recovering from a strained right calf when he suffered another injury, this time to his left calf, while running the bases.

Although the club has yet to confirm it officially, there is a possibility that Stanton could miss the remainder of the season.

He is no longer the dominant hitter he once was, but his power remains a valuable asset for an offense that has struggled with consistency. If he is unable to return, the Yankees will lose an important piece of their lineup down the stretch.

Ryan McMahon may not be a headline-grabbing star, but his absence has also been felt.

The infielder continues to recover from a sprained left thumb , and all indications suggest he could return in September.

His left-handed power and ability to play third base, second base, and first base provide valuable versatility that could prove especially important during the postseason.

Clarke Schmidt (Tommy John surgery recovery)

Clarke Schmidt could emerge as one of the Yankees’ biggest X-factors in October.

The right-hander continues progressing in his recovery from Tommy John surgery , with a return potentially coming in September.

The expectation is that he will come back as a reliever, a role in which he could provide multiple high-leverage innings, especially when starters are unable to work deep into playoff games.

The biggest question will be how effective he can be after such a lengthy rehabilitation. If Schmidt returns to form, he could become a crucial piece in strengthening New York’s bullpen as the Yankees chase another World Series title.

articles.body:
There is no rivalry hotter in Major League Baseball than Yankees vs. Red Sox , and this time it comes with an extra layer of tension: both teams are deeply involved in the fight for a postseason berth in the American League East.

In the overall standings, the New York Yankees are in sixth place in the Majors with a record of 74 wins and 57 losses, just ahead of their archrivals. The Boston Red Sox appear right behind them, in seventh place, with 73 wins and 59 losses.

Within the American League East, the picture is even tighter: the Tampa Bay Rays are on top, the Yankees are second, and the Red Sox are third . In other words, every game in this series is worth double, because a sweep could completely reshape the October conversation.

As for recent form, the Bronx Bombers come in with ups and downs : they were coming off a sweep in Baltimore and had dominated Toronto at home, but fell 7-9 to Houston on August 25 in an open hitting duel.

Boston, meanwhile, comes in on a roll: it won its last four games, including a sweep of the San Francisco Giants and two straight wins in Miami. The Red Sox have their bats on fire.

The first pitch in the New York vs Boston series is scheduled for this Friday, August 28, 2026, 7:15 p.m. Eastern Time (6:15 p.m. Central Time and 4:15 p.m. Pacific Time) , at the legendary Yankee Stadium in the Bronx, New York, a venue with a capacity of 47,309 fans.

It will be the start of the series between these two historic teams; the rest of the games in the series will have the following schedule :

Yankees vs Red Sox Game 3

For the local audience and across the rest of the United States, the matchup will be available via MLB.tv and on Apple TV, the same platform internationally.

Boston is the most productive offense in this matchup: the Red Sox have scored 600 runs against 495 allowed this season, for a +105 run differential.

New York’s rotation boasts big names such as Gerrit Cole, Max Fried, Carlos Rodón, and Luis Gil, while the bullpen relies on closers of the caliber of David Bednar and Camilo Doval.

Boston answers with a starting pitching staff led by Garrett Crochet, Sonny Gray, Ranger Suárez, and Brayan Bello, plus a luxury veteran at closer: 38-year-old Cuban Aroldis Chapman, who knows very well what it means to pitch in the Bronx.

In the New York offense, catcher Austin Wells stands out as a key piece of the lineup. On Boston's side, Japanese designated hitter Masataka Yoshida brings contact and experience, while Venezuelan catcher Carlos Narváez has been a pleasant surprise.

With rotations loaded with quality arms on both sides, this series promises pitching duels as much as fireworks with the bat.

articles.title: Aaron Judge potential return plan could be the gamble the Yankees need for another World Series run
articles.standfirst: Yankees manager Aaron Boone expects Aaron Judge to return on September 10 against the Rockies
articles.summary: Yankees manager Aaron Boone expects Aaron Judge to return on September 10 against the Rockies
articles.body:
The New York Yankees enter the final month of the regular season looking to solidify their positioning atop the American League wild-card picture, maintaining a comfortable cushion that all but guarantees October baseball in the Bronx.

Yet, navigating the summer months hasn’t been easy for manager Aaron Boone 's squad, primarily due to the prolonged absence of three-time MVP Aaron Judge . Sidelined since May 31 due to a severe stress fracture in his right first rib , Judge left a massive void in an offense that missed his stellar production, highlighted by 17 home runs and a .907 OPS across his first 59 games of the year.

While the supporting cast has fought hard to keep the ship afloat, securing the ultimate goal of another World Series run heavily depends on getting their captain back onto the diamond before the postseason lights turn on.

Balancing Lineup Depth and Defensive Value Upon Aaron Judge's Return

As the organization maps out Judge’s anticipated return to action in September , a fascinating roster dilemma has emerged concerning trade-deadline pickup Luis García Jr. García has been a revelation since arriving in the Bronx, providing an essential offensive spark that manager Aaron Boone desperately needed during the dog days of summer.

However, if the Yankees choose to shelter Judge by deploying him exclusively as the designated hitter out of an abundance of caution regarding his ribs, they risk accidentally freezing out one of their hottest bats.

The optimal configuration to keep García's bat firing in the starting nine requires sliding Judge back to his customary spot in right field. While protecting a player coming off a major structural injury is always a priority, putting Judge back on the grass makes tactical sense.

After all, Judge is not a defensive liability ; he has consistently ranked among the premier defensive right fielders in Major League Baseball , displaying a Gold Glove -caliber presence that completely changes the geometry of opposing base running.

Ultimately, shielding a superstar completely from every element of physical contact is an impossible game in professional sports. Judge could just as easily absorb an awkward jolt sliding into a bag or tracking down a gap shot, meaning the front office must weigh pure health management against maximizing their lineup's firepower.

The Yankees would rather play a slightly rusty Judge in right field than use him only as DH, since that would throw off the lineup. That September gamble could be what turns them from playoff contenders into World Series champs.

They have scored only 553 runs while allowing 632, for a negative run differential of -79. In short: they score little and allow too much, the worst possible combination when facing an offense like New York's.

The gap is decisive: a difference of 25 games in the win column between one and the other.

Odds analysis for Yankees vs Angels

The market reflects that imbalance without hesitation:

New York Yankees (moneyline): odds of 1.79, adjusted implied probability of 55.6%.

Los Angeles Angels (moneyline): odds of 2.17, adjusted implied probability of 44.4%.

The total runs line (over/under) is set at 8.5, with the over paying 1.86 and the under at 2.07. On the run line, the Yankees appear as -1.5 run favorites at 2.2, while the Angels at +1.5 are priced at 1.79.

This is where it makes sense to pause. The Yankees being only 1.79 favorites on the board seems generous considering the real gap between the two rosters.

Anaheim's home-field advantage tightens the price a bit, but the genuine value is not so much in the straight moneyline as in the run line: with a New York offense capable of punishing an Angels pitching staff that has allowed the aforementioned 632 runs, the over 8.5 looks enticing.

The market sees the Yankees as winners; we also see a game with runs.

We expect the Yankees to set the pace early. Their offense has the patience to work counts, draw walks, and punish any location mistakes by the Angels' starting pitchers, who have struggled to keep opponents in the park all season. New York should take the lead in the early innings and manage it with a clearly superior bullpen.

The Angels, playing at home, have the obligation to make the most of their crowd support and scratch out runs over a couple of innings, but their offensive production — the lowest in the American League West — suggests it will not be enough to cause an upset. We see the Angels scoring some, perhaps three runs, but without the ability to sustain the exchange.

New York Yankees run line -1.5 at odds of 2.20. It’s the highest-value play on the board. The difference in level between the two teams —25 games in the win column— justifies asking the Yankees to win by more than one run, and the 2.20 odds reward that conviction much better than the 1.79 moneyline.

As for the alternative bets, these are:

Over 8.5 runs at odds of 1.86. The Angels' pitching has allowed 632 runs this season; facing New York's offense, the game looks likely to go over the line comfortably.

New York Yankees moneyline at odds of 1.79. The more conservative option: if you prefer to avoid the 1.5-run spread and only want the visitors to win, the price still offers a reasonable return given New York's superiority.

They closed the series against the Boston Red Sox with a better-than-expected 16-1 win on August 30 and a commanding 9-2 victory, and in their recent streak they have piled up significant wins such as 6-1 and 5-3 over Baltimore and 8-3 against Toronto. Their offense has been exploding: double-digit runs in several games over the past month.

The Angels, meanwhile, are going through a nightmare. They are coming off being swept by the Philadelphia Phillies at home — 3-5, 2-4, and 1-4 losses — and they can barely get back on their feet. In their last ten appearances they have barely managed to salvage a handful of wins, among them that striking 18-3 over Houston on August 21, which stood out as an anomaly within a clearly negative trend.

Both rosters arrive complete according to the information available so far, with no significant absences reported. The Angels support their rotation with names like Japan's Yusei Kikuchi, Dominican José Soriano, Reid Detmers, and Grayson Rodriguez, along with veteran Kirby Yates (39 years old) and Ben Joyce's electric arm in the bullpen. The away moneyline at 1.75 is a short but reasonable price: the Yankees are not only a much superior team in the standings (26 more wins than Anaheim), but they also come in with their bats on fire.

That said, in baseball the variability of a single game always opens the door to a surprise, and 2.22 for the home team is not an absurd lottery if Anaheim sends its best arm to the mound. The real value, however, still lies with the Bronx.

articles.title: Aaron Judge’s ahead-of-schedule return puts the Yankees back in the World Series conversation
articles.standfirst: Aaron Judge is nearing his return, and the Yankees could soon get their biggest offensive weapon back.
articles.summary: Aaron Judge is nearing his return, and the Yankees could soon get their biggest offensive weapon back.
articles.body:
The New York Yankees began a week-long West Coast road trip on Monday with Aaron Judge traveling with the team, a positive sign in his recovery process and not just an opportunity for the captain to return to his home state.

If his progress continues in the right direction and he is able to increase his workload over the next few days, Judge could return to the Yankees’ lineup during their next homestand, scheduled for September 8-13 , manager Aaron Boone acknowledged.

“I’m not going to put a date on it, but I think those things are in play now,” Boone said before opening a series at Angel Stadium . “It’s about getting the durability and the workload built up on him, which is the biggest thing now.”

Judge was in right field during Monday’s batting practice session, taking part in defensive drills. The two-time American League MVP has been hitting indoors over the past week, still without facing high-velocity pitches, but he has responded well in his recovery from a right rib stress fracture that has kept him sidelined since late May.

The Yankees slugger hopes to avoid a minor league rehab assignment and make up for that step by facing live pitching with the Trajekt machine , a device that replicates the pitches of Major League pitchers.

“He’s doing well,” Boone said. “He’s here to continue to ramp up baseball activities. We’re getting closer, but we feel good about where he’s at.”

Judge’s return would provide a major boost for a Yankees team looking to regain consistency during the final stretch of the season and enter the playoff race with one of its biggest stars back in the lineup.
